problem: The shared website lane was blocked by two unrelated baseline defects: cms-admin overwrote the single-element selector helper with the query-all helper, and the homepage toggle regression depended on physical pointer hit-testing that was intermittently intercepted by unrelated overlays.
root_cause: CMS used the same selector variable for querySelector and querySelectorAll, so event binding received arrays. The toggle regression conflated state-transition correctness with pointer-overlay geometry already covered by separate visual/browser contracts.
decision: Keep single and multi CMS selector helpers distinct. Test homepage tab state transitions through deterministic DOM activation while leaving overlay and geometry validation to dedicated visual regression contracts.
prevention: CMS single-element event binding always uses querySelector.
CMS collection iteration always uses querySelectorAll.
Homepage toggle regression validates state transitions independently from unrelated overlays.
Dedicated visual regression remains responsible for occlusion and geometry.
